content:
Omar Siddiqui: Welcome to the sprint 23 retro. Let's start with what went well, then what didn't.
Hannah Lee: Went well: the new deploy pipeline saved us a lot of time this sprint.
Raj Patel: What slowed us down was the flaky integration tests. We lost probably two days re-running CI.
Elena Rossi: And the requirements for the reporting feature changed mid-sprint, which caused a lot of rework. Honestly that was frustrating.
Omar Siddiqui: Okay, let's agree on changes. Proposal one: we quarantine flaky tests automatically instead of re-running the whole pipeline. Everyone okay with that?
Raj Patel: Yes.
Kofi Mensah: Yes, makes sense.
Omar Siddiqui: Two: requirements are frozen once the sprint starts, and any change goes to the next sprint. Agreed?
Hannah Lee: Agreed.
Kofi Mensah: Agreed.
Omar Siddiqui: Three: let's try pair programming on all database migrations next sprint as an experiment.
Raj Patel: Good idea, let's do it.
Omar Siddiqui: Four: we're moving the retro to Thursday afternoons from now on.
Elena Rossi: Works for everyone.
Raj Patel: I'll write up the flaky test quarantine runbook by Monday.
Hannah Lee: I'll set up the pairing rotation schedule for next sprint.
Omar Siddiqui: Kofi, please create a dashboard tracking flaky test rates.
Omar Siddiqui: Elena, can you document the requirements freeze policy in the team wiki?
Hannah Lee: Raj, please tag the five flakiest tests so we can quarantine them first.
Omar Siddiqui: Kofi, can you move the retro calendar invite to Thursday?
Elena Rossi: Omar, please share the freeze policy with the product managers.
Kofi Mensah: One concern: if we quarantine too many tests, we could ship regressions without noticing.
Omar Siddiqui: Good point, we'll keep an eye on it. Thanks all.
